name: Arrays
summary: Use indexed storage to reason about scans, ordering, and in-place transformations.
interviewUse: Arrays are the base representation for many search, window, pointer, and dynamic-programming problems.
complexityFocus: Know when a single pass, sorting pass, or auxiliary map changes the time-space tradeoff.

name: Strings
summary: Treat text as structured sequences with encoding, frequency, and substring constraints.
interviewUse: String questions often test careful indexing and a pattern such as a window, trie, or frequency map.
complexityFocus: Account for repeated slicing, immutable string construction, and alphabet-size assumptions.

name: Hash Maps
summary: Trade memory for fast membership, counting, grouping, and lookup.
interviewUse: Maps often remove a nested loop by storing exactly the state needed for a future lookup.
complexityFocus: Explain average-case lookup and recognize when ordering or collisions alter the choice.
commonMistakes: Updating counts in the wrong order

name: Sorting
summary: Create useful order so neighboring values, intervals, or greedy choices become visible.
interviewUse: Sorting can simplify a problem even when it raises the running time to O(n log n).
complexityFocus: Separate comparison cost from the scan after sorting and state whether input mutation is allowed.
commonMistakes: Sorting when linear counting is simpler

name: Stacks & Queues
summary: Model last-in-first-out and first-in-first-out work explicitly.
interviewUse: Stacks capture unresolved history; queues organize breadth-first processing and streaming order.
complexityFocus: Understand amortized operations and avoid hidden linear front removals in array-backed queues.

name: Linked Lists
summary: Manipulate node relationships without relying on indexed access.
interviewUse: Linked-list tasks test pointer ownership, invariants, and handling of the head and tail.
complexityFocus: Distinguish O(1) rewiring from O(n) traversal and state whether extra nodes are allowed.
commonMistakes: Comparing values instead of node identity

name: Trees
summary: Reason recursively about hierarchical structure and subtree information.
interviewUse: Tree interviews combine traversal choice with a precise invariant returned from each subtree.
complexityFocus: Count each visited node and include recursion or explicit-stack height in space analysis.
commonMistakes: Confusing node count with tree height

name: Heaps
summary: Maintain access to an evolving minimum or maximum without fully sorting everything.
interviewUse: Heaps suit top-k selection, streaming priorities, and merging ordered sources.
complexityFocus: Know build-heap, push, and pop costs and compare a size-k heap with full sorting.

name: Tries
summary: Index strings by shared prefixes when prefix operations are central.
interviewUse: Tries make prefix existence and controlled character branching explicit.
complexityFocus: Express operations in terms of word length and discuss alphabet-dependent memory.
commonMistakes: Using a trie for plain exact lookup

name: Graphs
summary: Model entities and relationships, then traverse while controlling revisits and state.
interviewUse: Graph questions test representation, traversal, dependency reasoning, and component structure.
complexityFocus: Use O(V + E) for adjacency traversal and include queue, stack, or disjoint-set storage.

name: Backtracking
summary: Explore a decision tree while restoring state after each choice.
interviewUse: Backtracking fits enumeration under constraints when partial choices can be pruned.
complexityFocus: Describe branching factor, depth, output size, and the cost of copying versus mutation.

name: Dynamic Programming
summary: Reuse overlapping subproblem results under a clearly defined state and transition.
interviewUse: DP questions reward precise state definitions more than memorized recurrence formulas.
complexityFocus: Multiply the number of states by transition cost and identify reducible dimensions.
commonMistakes: Choosing a state that lacks needed context
Optimizing space before proving the recurrence

name: Binary Search
summary: Repeatedly discard an ordered half while preserving a search invariant.
interviewUse: Binary search applies to sorted collections and monotonic answer spaces.
complexityFocus: State the interval convention and prove why each update makes progress.

name: Intervals
summary: Represent ranges and reason about overlap, ordering, and coverage.
interviewUse: Interval problems usually become manageable after sorting by a meaningful endpoint.
complexityFocus: Include sorting cost and define whether touching endpoints overlap.
commonMistakes: Comparing against the wrong merged boundary

name: Greedy
summary: Make a locally optimal choice only when an exchange or invariant argument supports it.
interviewUse: Greedy problems test proof, not simply choosing the largest or smallest visible item.
complexityFocus: Often sorting dominates; explain why revisiting an earlier choice is unnecessary.

name: Bit Manipulation
summary: Use binary representation for compact state, parity, masks, and algebraic cancellation.
interviewUse: Bit operations can expose invariants that are harder to see with arithmetic or collections.
complexityFocus: State integer width and language-specific signed-shift behavior.
commonMistakes: Using bit tricks without explaining them
